«Você é uma pessoa boa.» (you catch 'boa' — good) You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «Há quantos dias estamos aqui?» (you catch 'dias' — days)
Asel laughs — with you, mostly. "Good try! Again — Combinado." They walk you through it, patient as sunrise.
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I said something cruel. I think about it every day."
Gianna has an edge today — something curdled.
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
"Take your time."
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"Still on that question."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Que lugar é este? Onde estamos?» (you catch 'Onde' — where) "Hello?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Isso mesmo, você acertou em cheio.» (That's it, you hit it right on. — you're fairly sure) They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
«Você é um anjo, obrigado de coração.» (You're an angel, thanks from the heart. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Não vou esquecer.» (I won't forget. — you're fairly sure) You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You lean in, catching the rise and fall of it. «Onde a gente dorme aqui?» (Where do we sleep here? — you're fairly sure)
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said fun was just being around your people. Do we count? Are we trying?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
A pause. When they speak again, it's about something else entirely.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Gianna grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Still on that personal stuff. We all learn."

lines: d38: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Yesenia Salazar is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d38: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d38: 🕯️ Yesenia is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d38: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d38: 🕯️ Yesenia Salazar is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d38: What Yesenia kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d38: "Yesenia's gone." Jacob looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Yesenia." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d38: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Aurora blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d38: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d38: 📖 LEARNED: Research & Records (Level 1). Find information fast: indexes, archives, and asking the right question.
d38: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d38: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Yesenia Salazar, 38 days. The mantle passes to Aurora Nguyen.
d38: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Aurora Nguyen, 35 — a librarian. Their hands know different work now: Night Eyes, Lucky Rock, Trophy Room, Bloodhound.
d38: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Stalker of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d38: The village's quarrel was with Yesenia — and Yesenia is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.

d38: The fire knew Aurora before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
